title: Print a loop nest
prompt: Write skeleton(loops: list[tuple[str, str]], body: str) -> str. Given loops outermost first, each a (variable, bound) pair, return C with one for (int32_t v = 0; v < bound; v++) { per loop, the body innermost, and a } per loop. Indent two spaces per level. Join lines with "\n", with no trailing newline. With no loops, return the body unchanged. The examples print each line break as \n.
starter:
def skeleton(loops: list[tuple[str, str]], body: str) -> str:
    """Nest one for loop per (variable, bound), outermost first, with the body innermost.
    Indent two spaces per level. Join lines with "\n", no trailing newline."""
    return body
hints: Build a list of lines and join it with "\n".join(lines). The lines are: one for header per loop, the body, then one } per loop.
Loop number d (0 for the outermost) is indented 2*d spaces. The body is indented 2*n. The closing braces count back down from 2*(n-1) to 0.
enumerate(loops) gives you the depth for each header, and " " * d makes the padding. In an f-string, write a literal brace as {{.
explain: A renderer prints loops by recursion or, as here, by counting depth. Getting the closers to mirror the headers is the whole trick. The examples print each line break as \n so a whole nest fits on one line.
